Controls
Musical examples

Use Panic when a MIDI device holds a note that will not stop.

If new notes must not follow, stop playback with Play/Stop (1,8). This is optional; Panic does not stop the sequencer.
Hold the navigation button of a page you are not on for about a second. For example, with Song showing, hold Channel (3,8).
Release the button after the Note Off sweep. The selected page does not change.

Panic sends Note Off for every note on every MIDI channel and connected device. Holding the selected page button does not trigger Panic.

Panic does not stop the sequencer or cancel scheduled strum or arpeggio voices. Playback and scheduled voices continue, so new notes can sound during or after the sweep. Use Play/Stop to stop playback.

04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Channel panic gesture

Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

Open Song at (6,8), so Channel is an inactive page button.
Hold Channel at (3,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use Silence a sounding note for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.

RECIPE 02
Silence connected MIDI notes from Song view with the Pattern panic gesture

Use this on a connected MIDI instrument when a note is stuck. The panic gesture sends note-release messages to connected MIDI outputs, but it does not stop the sequencer. The manual’s captured Output strip replays a recorded result; it does not send messages to your instrument.

Open Song at (6,8), so Pattern is an inactive page button.
Hold Pattern at (5,8) until the panic gesture fires, then release. The page remains Song.
A stuck MIDI note should stop; inspect the release messages in Output. The sequencer keeps running, so new notes may still play. Press Stop separately if you want silence to continue.

Use Silence a sounding note for the long-note comparison. The other examples show the gesture from a silent project.

Step 3: From Song, hold the Channel button (3,8) for about two seconds, then release it. Panic sends Note Off to the connected MIDI outputs to release stuck notes. Open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. It holds Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches (degree, rotations, transpose). They change what a MIDI keyboard plays and records on the selected channel: with mapping Off the keyboard plays its own notes, and with mapping On the white keys play the selected scale, optionally shaped by the Scale Editor's degree, rotation and transposition.

04 / MUSICAL EXAMPLES
Musical examples
RECIPE 01
Map an external keyboard through the scale’s rotated degrees

Goal: compare the same incoming MIDI keys with Honour scale rotations Off and On. Map scale to white keys places the selected scale on the keyboard’s white keys; the Honour switches control whether the Scale Editor’s degree, rotation and transpose settings affect that mapping.

Baseline: in PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control, set Map scale to white keys On. In the Scale Editor select C natural minor, set degree II, rotation 2 and global transpose +2. Set Honour scale degree On, Honour scale rotations Off and Honour scale transpose Off. Play MIDI keys 60 through 72 chromatically at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 68, 68, 70, 70, 72, 72, 74.
Rotation comparison: turn Honour scale rotations On and replay MIDI keys 60 through 72 at velocity 90. Output: 62, 63, 63, 65, 65, 67, 6

visibleLinks.text:
Honor Scale Rotations
Apply scale rotation to mapped MIDI keyboard input. Default: Off.

Honor Scale Degree
Apply scale degree to mapped MIDI keyboard input. Default: Off.

stepLabels: Step 1: Channel 1 plays a four-step pattern, C3 D3 E3 F3 (MIDI 60, 62, 64, 65) at velocities 127, 117, 107 and 97, through the test MIDI device at 90 BPM with Rate /1 and channel range steps 1-4. The sequencer is stopped and a MIDI keyboard is connected as Mosaic's input. Every Mosaic option is at its default, so Map scale to white keys and the three Honour switches are Off, and the Scale Editor is on C major.

Step 2: Play some keys on the keyboard: each sounds the note you pressed, because nothing is mapped yet. Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Map scale to white keys and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.
Step 3: Close the menu and play the white keys from C3 up to C4 on the keyboard. In C major they sound as written: 60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71, 72. The MIDI strip lists the notes Mosaic sent.
Step 4: Open the Scale Editor (grid (4,8)), turn E3 two detents and press K3. The Scale row reads Minor, natural minor.
Step 5: Return to the Channel editor (3,8) and play the white keys again: they now follow C natural minor, 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72 (C D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C).
Step 6: Open the Scale Editor (4,8) again, turn E2 one click to Degree, turn E3 one detent and press K3. Degree reads ii°. Degree picks which scale note the keyboard's C starts on.
Step 7: Turn E2 to the Rotation row, turn E3 two detents and press K3. Rotation reads r2. Rotation moves the top keys down an octave.

Step 8: Tap the global transpose fader on the grid at its lowest value, then tap its increment button fourteen times, and return to the Channel editor (3,8). The Scale overview lists Transpose +2, which shifts everything.
Step 9: The three Honour switches are still Off, so none of this is applied yet: the white keys still play 60, 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72.
Step 10: Tap K1 and open PARAMS > MOSAIC > Midi control. Select Honour scale degree and turn E3 right to On. The row reads On.

Step 11: Close the menu and play C3 to C4 again. Key C now plays the scale's second note: 62, 63, 65, 67, 68, 70, 72, 74 (D E-flat F G A-flat B-flat C D). Rotation and transpose stay unapplied, so you can start a phrase from degree II without changing the scale.
